Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This pattern needs steady pressure control and fine line work, so it is best attempted after practising simpler designs.
In Berber tradition, specific geometric henna symbols carry protective meanings against the evil eye. The Hamsa (Hand of Fatima) is a common Moroccan henna motif symbolizing protection and blessings.

faq.q: What makes Moroccan henna different?
faq.a: Moroccan henna features bold geometric and tribal patterns derived from Berber traditions, unlike the floral styles of Arabic and Indian henna.

faq.q: Do Moroccan henna designs have meanings?
faq.a: Yes, many Berber geometric symbols carry specific meanings — diamonds represent femininity, triangles provide protection, and the hamsa wards off the evil eye.

faq.q: Is Moroccan henna paste different?
faq.a: Moroccan henna paste is known for being exceptionally pure and fine. Fez and Marrakech are famous for producing high-quality henna powder.

title: Artistic Moroccan Bell Garland Mehndi Design for Front Hand
descriptionParagraphs: An exquisite moroccan mehndi design tailored for the palm, featuring lotus pattern and peacock motif. Rated as Expert, this pattern is perfect for an engagement.

The palm has the thickest skin on the hand, so henna stains darkest here. Keep the hand open and relaxed while the paste dries so the lines do not crack or smudge. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

Moroccan henna traditions are rooted in Berber culture, with designs varying between regions like Fez, Marrakech, and the Atlas Mountains. In Morocco, henna is applied at the 'Night of the Henna' (Laylat al-Henna) three days before the wedding.

Application tips: Bold, even line work is essential for the Moroccan aesthetic — practice straight lines extensively. Leave the paste on for at least four to six hours; the longer it stays, the deeper the stain.
